chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Mihran from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'When a man is in the mosque during prayer and wishes to spit, he should spit to his left.' And if he is not in prayer, 'he should not spit directly in front of the qibla, but should spit to his right and left.'
ai.seo_question: Where should a Muslim spit in the mosque during and outside of prayer?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the general etiquette of cleanliness (*adab*) within the sacred space of the mosque. It distinguishes between the mechanical constraints of prayer, where spitting to the left is prescribed to avoid disturbing the line of prostration, and general conduct, which prohibits spitting directly in front of the Qibla to maintain reverence for the direction of worship. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving the sanctity and purity of the mosque as a place of divine encounter.
